title: Digital Bridges for Community Learning

partners.name: Fictional Aegean Community Learning Association
partners.role: Coordinator; consortium governance, financial consolidation and inclusive recruitment
partners.contribution: Community outreach, accessible facilitation and a local pilot cohort; maintains the joint decision and risk registers.

partners.name: Fictional Ponte Adult Education Cooperative
partners.contribution: Participatory needs research, assessment design and cross-country evidence synthesis; checks that learning outcomes are comparable.

partners.name: Fictional Puente Digital Learning Foundation
partners.contribution: Accessible resource production, facilitator development and adoption support; manages the public resource repository.

rationale: The consortium hypothesises that adults with limited digital confidence encounter practical barriers when accessing community information and learning services. It also hypothesises that small adult-learning providers lack adaptable, accessible teaching sequences. These are design assumptions, not findings from a completed survey. WP2 will test them through interviews with {interviews} adults, facilitator consultations and an accessibility review before curriculum production is finalised. If the evidence identifies different priorities, the steering group will adjust activities within the agreed objectives and resources rather than treating the initial assumptions as established facts.
european_added_value: Partners will co-design one shared competence framework, test it in different community settings and compare implementation evidence using a common rubric. Each partner will peer-review another partner's materials before local adaptation. The expected added value is a documented distinction between transferable teaching principles and country-specific service examples; a single-country pilot would not supply that comparison. This is a proposed benefit to evaluate, not an already demonstrated result.
target_group: Adults aged 25 and over who want practical digital skills for everyday learning and community participation, with priority outreach to people facing financial, geographical, accessibility or confidence barriers. Participation will not depend on owning a device. The project plans {learners} unique adult learners and {facilitators} facilitators. The {interviews} interviewees and {codesign} co-design participants will be subsets of the adult learner pool, not extra people added to the reach total. Each partner will use a coded participant register to prevent double counting across activities.

objectives.text: By M6, agree a tested needs model and common outcome rubric, using {interviews} adult interviews and co-design with {codesign} adults across the consortium.
By M12, publish six accessible learning units in partner languages and English and prepare {facilitators} facilitators to deliver and assess them.

By M20, offer {pilot_hours} learning hours to {learners} unique adults, aiming for at least {completions} completions and a mean gain of {skill_gain_pp} percentage points on paired practical assessments.

By M24, secure documented adoption plans from {external_adopters} external providers and record {resource_visits} unique resource-page visits, while preserving separate counts for learners, providers and website usage.

activities.title: Agree the operating model
activities.description: Confirm partner responsibilities, internal transfer arrangements, quality gates and escalation routes. Create a common evidence folder and decision log. No fictional partnership agreement is presented as signed.
activities.deliverable: D1.1 consortium operating manual and evidence register
activities.acceptance: All partner leads review the manual; unresolved commitments are logged with an owner and due date.

activities.title: Monitor delivery and resources
activities.description: Hold monthly operational calls and quarterly steering reviews. Compare deliverables, recruitment, assessment quality and resource use against the plan. Record changes and keep a reserve recruitment route without increasing claimed participant totals.
activities.deliverable: D1.2 quarterly delivery dashboards and final consolidation
activities.acceptance: Each review records progress, decisions, open risks and supporting evidence; project changes are authorised before implementation.

activities.title: Test the needs assumptions
activities.description: Interview {interviews} adults and consult facilitators using a shared protocol. Map existing resources before proposing new ones. Record sampling limitations and contrary findings instead of inventing national prevalence statistics.
activities.deliverable: D2.1 country needs briefs and cross-country synthesis
activities.acceptance: Evidence is traceable to consented, minimised research records and explicitly separates observations from interpretations.

activities.title: Co-design outcomes and accessibility
activities.description: Involve {codesign} adults from the planned learner pool in local workshops. Agree practical tasks, a common assessment rubric and adaptations for language, literacy and device-access needs.
activities.deliverable: D2.2 outcome framework, accessibility checklist and pilot protocol
activities.acceptance: Each partner and an adult participant panel reviews the framework; the steering group approves the curriculum brief at M6.

activities.title: Develop six practical units
activities.description: Prototype accessible units on trusted information, communication, safe accounts, learning services, everyday problem solving and civic participation. Early prototyping may start in M5, but release criteria are frozen only after the M6 needs gate.
activities.deliverable: D3.1 facilitator guide, learner materials and assessment tasks
activities.acceptance: A partner other than the author reviews each unit; accessibility issues are fixed before pilot use.

activities.title: Prepare facilitators
activities.description: Prepare {facilitators} facilitators through blended practice and moderated assessment. They rehearse support for low-confidence learners and agree how to score the same practical task consistently.
activities.deliverable: D3.2 facilitator practice records and moderation notes
activities.acceptance: Facilitators demonstrate the delivery and assessment rubric before pilot cohorts open in M11.

activities.title: Refine the first delivery version
activities.description: Use early delivery observations to refine instructions without changing the outcome rubric mid-comparison. Maintain version numbers and document the reasons for edits.
activities.acceptance: All published units include language/version information, reuse conditions and an accessibility contact.

activities.title: Deliver supported learning cohorts
activities.description: Offer {pilot_hours} learning hours to {learners} unique adults. Provide accessible materials and agreed device support. Aim to include at least {fewer_opportunities} participants facing the defined access barriers. Take baseline and final practical assessments with the same rubric.
activities.deliverable: D4.1 attendance, completion and paired-assessment dataset
activities.acceptance: Completion means attending at least 80% of planned hours and attempting the final practical task; missing assessments and withdrawals remain visible.

activities.title: Analyse outcomes and transfer limits
activities.description: Compare paired results by site, describe attrition and inspect differences between groups where reporting is safe. The target is {completions} completions and {skill_gain_pp} percentage points mean improvement; these are ambitions, not guaranteed findings.
activities.deliverable: D4.2 evaluation report and adaptation recommendations
activities.acceptance: The report gives denominators, missing-data counts and limitations; it makes no causal impact claim without an appropriate design.

activities.title: Share usable results
activities.description: Publish versioned resources and hold practice-focused demonstrations through adult-learning networks, including EPALE where appropriate. Target {resource_visits} unique resource-page visits and record them separately from participant reach.
activities.deliverable: D5.1 open resource collection and dissemination evidence log
activities.acceptance: Resources have reuse information, accessible formats and a working feedback route; outreach counts identify their measurement method.

activities.title: Secure adoption and ownership
activities.description: Support {external_adopters} external providers to prepare adoption plans. Agree which partner maintains each resource, who covers post-grant hosting and how adaptations are reviewed after project completion.
activities.deliverable: D5.2 adoption plans and twelve-month maintenance commitments
activities.acceptance: Each plan names an owner, intended delivery setting, resources and review date; unsigned intentions remain labelled as such.

risks.risk: Recruitment fails to reach adults facing access barriers
risks.trigger: A site's confirmed enrolments remain below 70% of its plan four weeks before delivery
risks.mitigation: Activate community referral routes, offer alternative session times and device support; retain the same eligibility and de-duplication rules.

risks.risk: Different assessors score the same task inconsistently
risks.trigger: Moderation identifies a difference above one rubric level
risks.mitigation: Repeat calibration with common examples and double-score a sample before publishing pooled results.

risks.trigger: A participant cannot complete a core task with the supplied format or support
risks.mitigation: Provide an accessible alternative promptly, log the barrier and test the correction with affected users before wider release.

risks.risk: Cost assumptions or partner capacity prove unrealistic
risks.trigger: A quarterly review forecasts a material resource shortfall or a missed milestone
risks.mitigation: Replan delivery and seek the required approvals; do not silently remove agreed activities or substitute an unsupported grant amount.

risks.trigger: Identifiable information appears in a shared report or access permissions fail review
risks.mitigation: Restrict access, remove unnecessary identifiers, investigate the incident and follow the agreed local data-handling procedure.

assumptions: Every organisation and its capacity description in this fixture is fictional; no registry, OID, mandate or signature is represented as verified.
Learner demand, facilitator availability and the proposed access-barrier mix are planning assumptions to test during needs analysis.
Budget estimates are fictional internal planning figures, not supplier quotations or Erasmus+ unit-cost entitlements.
Partners are assumed to contribute EUR {cofinancing} from unrestricted organisational cash resources; written commitments are still missing.
Month numbers are relative project months. No open call, eligible start date, submission deadline or award is asserted.

missing_evidence.item: Legal identity, OIDs, coordinator establishment history and eligibility declarations
missing_evidence.reason: Fictional names and reported organisational ages do not establish legal eligibility.

missing_evidence.item: Signed partner roles, staff capacity and own-resource commitments
missing_evidence.reason: The plan currently assumes capacity and co-financing rather than documenting them.

missing_evidence.item: Traceable national/local needs evidence and participant consultations
missing_evidence.due: Before making factual claims in a real application
missing_evidence.reason: The rationale is a hypothesis, not a completed needs analysis.

missing_evidence.item: Cost basis, recruitment feasibility and accessibility support arrangements
missing_evidence.due: Before a real submission and pilot launch
missing_evidence.reason: Targets and resource estimates need operational validation.

missing_evidence.item: Current call, National Agency priorities, application form and complete selection/exclusion checks
missing_evidence.reason: This exercise uses a frozen 2026 guide snapshot and checks only a narrow rule subset.
